strengths: Well-motivated problem with clear identification of limitations in existing PRMs (isolated step modeling, limited outcome awareness)
Principled theoretical foundation using conditional probability and PBRS, with elegant decomposition linking process rewards to final outcome: S(T) = ∏(1-h(t)) = ∏e^rt
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across three downstream applications (Best-of-N, beam search, RL) on multiple datasets and model architectures with consistent improvements
Strong robustness properties empirically demonstrated: resistant to reward hacking, naturally encourages self-reflection, superior cross-sample comparability (AUPRC metric)
Achieves competitive/comparable performance without relying on verifiable rewards from ground truth, addressing scalability limitation of existing methods
Excellent data efficiency: reaches near-optimal with 50% of training data (Table 4), superior to PRM under same budgets (Table 14)
Thorough ablations, case studies, and analysis substantiating design choices, with extension to non-mathematical domains validated
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: primarily combines established techniques (conditional probability, PBRS from 1999); the 'wrong state' framing is pragmatic but somewhat incremental
Improvement magnitudes modest in key settings: Best-of-N typically +1-2%, RL without VR at 77.8% vs PQM 72% but still 4.6% below PURE+verifier (82.4%)

Training requires annotated step-level error positions (zi) for Lz loss; limited exploration of generalization beyond math (MMLU-Pro shows smaller gains); applicability to domains lacking fine-grained annotations unclear

Methodological clarity gaps: Why model complementary event vs. directly modeling S(t)? Transition from PBRS to training losses (Eq. 8→11-13) underexplained; three losses design choices not fully justified; fixed γ=1 not ablated
All baselines re-implemented by authors (potential implementation bias); recent methods (R-PRM, GenPRM) comparisons in appendix; official implementations would strengthen claims
Limited failure mode analysis: when/why does CRM underperform (Llama3.1-8B shows modest gains)? What reasoning patterns cause issues? No error analysis provided
Step definition sensitivity unexplored: assumes newline-separated steps; granularity impact on performance not ablated; could be significant for domains with ambiguous boundaries

Missing practical considerations: no computational efficiency analysis (inference time, memory), no hyperparameter sensitivity exploration beyond learning rate mention, limited discussion of token-level RLOO design criticality
